script: Am I the jerk for calling out coworker during a potluck. Yesterday we had a company potluck for our department, celebrating Tom's exit. We all piled up plates, then the usual ritual: leave the food out a bit, then stash it in the fridge for later munches. Most people had a dish, even Tom. But Bob—he's never been the one to bring anything. Never. When it was time to pack up, Bob pulls out a stack of Tupperware, starts filling them with everyone's food. I stopped him mid‑pour. "Yo, that's not yours. Why are you taking it?" he says, like it's normal. "I don't want to cook after my shift, so I am just grabbing some to take home." I could see the other people's eyes, like the audacity of it. "Maybe those who cooked it could bring it home instead," I said. He shrugged, kept filling the boxes, then snatched a couple packs of cookies left on the table and shoved them into his bag. I ran to the few coworkers who'd brought a lot. Their faces turned, they were visibly annoyed. "Did you see that? He just took it!" I said. I am not the first to call him out, but was I the jerk for calling him out? (Honestly, I was just keeping it real.)
